abjure

ab-JOOR · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To abjure is to formally renounce or swear off something, often under oath.

The convert was asked to abjure his former beliefs before joining the order.

Example

In open court, the witness abjured the false testimony she had given the year before.

This wasn't a quiet change of mind -- it was a formal, public renunciation made under oath, which is exactly abjure.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

renounce: To renounce is to give up or reject something openly and seriously — a claim, a habit, a title. To abjure goes further: you renounce the thing formally and publicly, often swearing it off under a real or symbolic oath. Every abjuring is a renouncing, but only the sworn, ceremonial kind earns the word abjure.

recant: To recant is to take back a specific statement or belief you previously voiced, admitting you no longer stand by it. To abjure looks forward instead: you formally swear off a belief or allegiance, oath and all, whether or not you ever preached it aloud. You recant what you said; you abjure what you held.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

embrace: accept something willingly and wholeheartedly

Where it sits · how formal and public the refusal — decline → abjure → disown

decline vs. abjure: Declining something is a simple, everyday refusal; abjuring it is a formal, often public renunciation.

disown vs. abjure: Disowning goes even further than abjuring: to abjure is to formally renounce a belief or claim, but to disown is to cast off a person entirely — a public, often legal severing meant to be permanent.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ab-

prefix — ab-: away, off (Latin)

root — jur

root — jur: to swear (Latin (jurare))

suffix — -e

suffix — -e: verb-forming ending (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Abjure comes from Latin ab- ('away') + jurare ('to swear') -- literally 'to swear away,' formally taking back a former oath or claim.

Use the root in a new word: jury

Use the root in a new word: jury: The same jurare root gives us jury (a group sworn to judge fairly) and perjury (lying under a sworn oath).
